exposure: Various reasons for ICU admission in obstetric patients
outcome: Interventions required (e.g., mechanical ventilation, blood transfusion)
cohort: 91 obstetric patients admitted to the ICU of a tertiary care teaching hospital in South India over a 2-year period
finding: Hypertensive disorders and obstetric hemorrhage were the most common reasons for ICU admission among obstetric patients, with a high proportion requiring interventions like mechanical ventilation and blood transfusions, and sepsis being a significant contributor to ICU mortality.
mod_finding: 47.3% of the patients underwent cesarean delivery.
